subject: SOC 2 exception: privileged access review — root cause, remediation plan, and evidence schedule
messages:
From: Amelia Reed <amelia.reed@datasafeinc.com>

Cc: security@datasafeinc.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2: follow-up on exception / evidence request

Olga —

Thanks for the call earlier. As part of our procurement security review for the upcoming contract, our audit team flagged the privileged access control exception noted in your Type II report covering 2025-06–2026-06. To close our internal gating item we need three things:

1) Short technical root cause for the exception (what allowed the lapse in quarterly privileged access reviews)
2) Management response with concrete remediation milestones and owner(s)
3) Interim evidence that the control is now running (logs, completed review checklist) or an approved bridge letter if timing prevents complete evidence delivery before our board meeting on 2026-09-08

Could you provide the RCA and a proposed evidence delivery schedule by end of week? If a signed bridge letter will be needed, please indicate who can sign on your side.

Appreciate it — this is the gating item for our security committee.

—Amelia Reed
Senior Security Analyst
DataSafe Inc.
amelia.reed@datasafeinc.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Amelia Reed <amelia.reed@datasafeinc.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2: follow-up on exception / evidence request

Amelia / Olga / team —

Root cause summary (concise):
- What happened: The quarterly privileged access review for a subset of service accounts was not executed for the 2026-Q2 cycle due to a combination of automation gap and a missing alert. Our internal scheduled job that compiles the review checklist failed after a schema change in an internal inventory table; the monitoring alert for that job was misconfigured and did not trigger escalation.

- Why it mattered: Without the generated checklist, the operational owner did not receive the prompt to run the manual verification steps for those service accounts. This resulted in an omission in the documented evidence for that quarter.

- Remediation taken (already completed):
  * Repaired the inventory schema transformer and re-ran the job (logs attached)
  * Restored and tested monitoring alerting with a synthetic failure test (screenshot of alert test in runbook)
  * Performed an immediate ad-hoc privileged access review covering the affected accounts; findings were low-risk and no unauthorized accounts were present

- Remediation planned (timeline & owners):
  * 2026-09-03: Deliver interim bridge letter and attach the ad-hoc review evidence + job run logs (owner: Markus Klein)
  * 2026-09-10: Formalize automation hardening checklist and add unit tests to inventory transformer (owner: Engineering SRE lead, Neha Kapoor)
  * 2026-09-17: Completed reconciliation package (signed reviewer checklists, reconciled logs) and auditor-facing summary (owner: Olga Petrov)

Attachments included in this message:
- privileged_access_root_cause_summary.pdf (2 pages — RCA + timeline)
- access_review_audit_log_2026-08.csv (redacted account ids)
- remediation_runbook_2026-08.md (steps taken + alert test screenshots referenced)

Notes on evidence: the ad-hoc review outputs include reviewer initials and timestamps; we have redacted service account identifiers in the CSV for security but can provide a view-only log link if your audit team needs full identifiers under an NDA.

If a signed bridge letter is required for your committee, Olga / Stephanie — I propose Olga or Stephanie sign; Stephanie please advise on procurement signatory acceptance.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: privileged_access_root_cause_summary.pdf; access_review_audit_log_2026-08.csv; remediation_runbook_2026-08.md
